To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we have isolated a cDNA clone encoding a protein with a high degree of identity to the rat TAG-1, (2) we have mapped this gene to chromosome 1q, and (3) we have identified a putative signal peptide and a putative GPI linkage site.
we isolated the cDNA and mapped the chromosomal location of the human gene encoding a cell adhesion protein involved in the formation of neuronal connections in the brain.
we isolated a cDNA encoding the human homolog of TAG-1 and that this cDNA was used to localize the gene to human chromosome 1q.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular biology of the TAG-1 gene and its protein product.
the isolation and characterization of the gene ( TAX1 ) encoding the axonal cell adhesion molecule TAG-1.
the isolation and molecular characterization of the human homologue (TAX1 gene) of the axonal cell adhesion molecule TAG-1.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the human gene for TAG-1 has been isolated, and that it is located on chromosome 1.
human TAG-1 is a cell surface protein that is expressed on neurons and is involved in axonal growth.
the human homolog of the chick axonin- 1 and the rat TAG-1 is TAX1, the cDNA for which is reported here.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified a human homologue of the axonal glycoproteins TAG-1 and have mapped the TAX1 gene to chromosome 1q31-q32.
we have cloned the human homologue to TAG-1 and have localized its chromosomal location.
the human gene for TAG-1 is highly similar to the rat and chick genes, that the gene is located on chromosome 1, and that the human TAG-1 gene may be useful in studying TAG-1 in humans.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the TAG-1 gene is highly conserved among vertebrate species.
the TAG-1 gene is a good candidate gene to investigate the role of TAG-1 in human neurodegenerative disorders.
the human gene encoding TAG-1, a cell adhesion protein involved in neurite outgrowth, is located on the long arm of chromosome 1.
